findings.title: Cleanup failure reports success while the servo remains enabled
findings.trigger: The five torque-off writes all raise; alternatively an error-status or bad-checksum reply has the expected length and servo ID.
findings.observed: All three negative mock cases return 0 and print the unconditional torque-off claim despite final torque=1. Error-status and bad-checksum replies stop cleanup after one attempt and restore torque cap from500 to1000 while torque remains enabled.
findings.suggested_correction: Validate response framing/length/checksum/status. Prove torque off before restoring a higher torque limit; return nonzero and report failure when cleanup cannot be verified. Ensure the factory caller propagates that failure.

existing_review_findings: Reviewer-lead comment6415199192 was read; previously reported print-FAIL continuation, stale mv, remote Ctrl-C and Tcl/IP issues were not relabelled as new findings.
limits: Host-only simulated serial responses; no actual motor, sound, microphone, reset, SSH or network-device validation.
The factory-lamp and make-prompts scripts were syntax checked only; neither was executed.
